name: OCRia-1
context_scaling: Inherited unchanged from Qwen/Qwen3.5-4B (config.json max_position_embeddings 262144). This derivative does not publish a context-extension recipe of its own.
attention_variant: Inherited unchanged from Qwen/Qwen3.5-4B: 8 full GQA layers (kv heads 4, head_dim 256) and 24 other layers, per the base config.json.
notes: ADDED 2026-11-28 (trending sweep). A finetune of Qwen/Qwen3.5-4B, not a new base model: same config.json (Qwen3_5ForConditionalGeneration, 32 layers, 8 full-attention + 24 linear-attention layers, head_dim 256, 4 kv heads, 262,144 native context). params_b 5.175 is safetensors.total 5,174,964,736 from the HF API and includes the vision tower, which the text-only base record (qwen3-5-4b, 4.66B) does not; active_params_b 4.66 is inherited from the base record's text-side count rather than re-derived, so it is a FLOOR, not a measurement. Recorded as a contender on size-class evidence, not base-vs-tuned delta: the card never scores Qwen3.5-4B on ParseBench, so every row below compares this 4B against OTHER parsers in the card's own tables (Infinity-Parser2-Pro 35B, LightOnOCR-3-4B, Chandra-OCR-2 4B, olmOCR-2 7B, KDL-Frontier-Parser-nano-v2). All numbers are the lab's own runs (LlamaIndex), hence vendor_claim; several competitors' cells are their published figures rather than re-runs, which the card states. LOSES: ParseBench 2 visual grounding 85.96 vs KDL-Frontier-Parser-nano-v2 88.28 (the one dimension of six it does not win), recorded below. Licence 'other' (LlamaIndex Community License), repo created 2026-11-13. Hardware gate: 5.175 x 0.5 = 2.6 GiB, active 4.66B <= 40.

benchmarks.name: ParseBench 2 (overall)
benchmarks.config: Card section 'Benchmarks', ParseBench 2 table column 'OCRia-1 (4B)'; 4,317 pages over 6 dimensions, run with the ocria_1 pipeline of run-llama/ParseBench (vLLM text + layout boxes), dataset revision 2d9a2344, parse-bench 2.2.1. Card's own rank: 7 of 61 overall, 1 of 23 open-weight. Same-table comparators: Infinity-Parser2-Pro (35B) 78.50, KDL-Frontier-Parser-nano-v2 80.13, LightOnOCR-3-4B 78.39. NO BASE COLUMN: the Qwen3.5-4B init is not scored on ParseBench anywhere on the card, so there is no base-vs-tuned delta for this row - the claim is size-class only (4B beats a 35B parser).

benchmarks.name: ParseBench 1 (overall)
benchmarks.config: Card section 'Benchmarks', summary table; 2,078 pages over 5 dimensions. Card rank 2 of 158 overall, 1 of 53 open-weight. Only the rank is printed, not a comparator column, so this row is quoted from the card without a same-table rival number. Includes visual grounding from the repo's layout boxes.

benchmarks.name: olmOCR-bench
benchmarks.config: Card table 'Model | olmOCR-bench | PulseBench-Tab | fr-bench-pdf2md', row 'OCRia-1 (4B)'; 1,288 px on the long side. Value is the mean of the three table and formula categories (Tables, arXiv math, Old scans math), per the card's footnote 1; other systems' cells are their published numbers. Comparators in the same table: Infinity-Parser2-Pro (35B) 90.2, LightOnOCR-3-4B 90.1, olmOCR-2 (7B) 83.1, Chandra-OCR-2 (4B) 89.4.

benchmarks.name: PulseBench-Tab
benchmarks.config: Same card table, row 'OCRia-1 (4B)'; crops capped at 2,560 px. Card reports the metric on a 0-1 scale in the report and multiplies by 100 here. Comparators: Infinity-Parser2-Pro (35B) 82, LightOnOCR-3-4B 82, dots.mocr (3B) 82, Surya OCR 2 (0.7B) 71.

benchmarks.name: ParseBench 2 (visual grounding dimension)
benchmarks.config: LOSES. Card ParseBench 2 per-dimension table, row 'OCRia-1 (4B)', Visual grounding column. KDL-Frontier-Parser-nano-v2 scores 88.28 in the same column (Infinity-Parser2-Pro 35B 87.04); OCRia-1 wins the other five dimensions (Text 87.87, Formatting 91.59, Tables 86.28, Charts 77.63, Forms 82.09) but not this one. Bounding-box quality from the repo's layout boxes is the recorded weak point.

benchmarks.name: fr-bench-pdf2md
benchmarks.config: Same card table, row 'OCRia-1 (4B)'; 2,048 px. Comparators: LightOnOCR-3-4B 71.4 (the closest), Chandra-OCR-2 (4B) 65.5, Infinity-Parser2-Pro (35B) 54.9, olmOCR-2 (7B) 56.9. The 4B model wins this column by 0.7 over the best other 4B and by 17.2 over the 35B parser.
